text:
jess: FYI - saw 2 OOMs in the prod inference canary pool over the last hour. No obvious alloc spam in the app logs. Posting baseline vm stats + small log snippet. Can someone triage short-lived memory spikes? :eyes:

ops-bot: [alert] container redwood/canary-43: OOM killed pid=3129 signal=9 cgroup=/dedicated-pool/canary-43

jess: snippet from kernel dmesg around the first OOM:
```
[12345.678901] Out of memory: Kill process 3129 (inference) score 997 or sacrifice child
[12345.678905] Killed process 3129 (inference) total-vm:20480000kB, anon-rss:17600000kB, file-rss:0kB, shmem-rss:0kB
```

omar: thanks — passing to runtime folks. Quick ask: can someone grab `pmap -x` + `cat /proc/<pid>/smaps` just before we restart? Also a `jeprof` dump (if jemalloc) or `pprof` if tcmalloc.

ryan: I can do the pmap/smaps on the next repro. Which machine and which pid do you want?

jess: canary-43 on gpunode-7. Current (dead) pid was 3129. If we can repro on the same image, do it against the repro harness: `./ops/bench/run_canary_load --tag canary-43 --steps 120` — that should reproduce the tail.

ana: quick thought: we changed MALLOC_ARENA_MAX for the canary last week in the runtime image (see #3241). Could be arena growth under high concurrency. Check `/etc/ld.so.preload` and env MALLOC_CONF.

omar: good call. Also check cgroup memory.high/swap.current limits. In a past case arenas + overcommit made rss balloon without reclaim.

ria (typo fixed to tia): adding a short command list to run when reproing locally:
```
# start workload
./ops/bench/run_canary_load --tag canary-43 --concurrency 12 --seq 2048
# in parallel (on the same host)
pid=$(pgrep -f inference)
echo $pid
sudo cat /proc/$pid/smaps > /tmp/smaps.$pid
sudo pmap -x $pid | tail -n 20
# jemalloc stats (if enabled)
echo 'stats' | nc -U /tmp/jemalloc.$pid.sock > /tmp/je_stats.$pid
# collect perf samples
sudo perf record -F 99 -p $pid -g -- sleep 30
sudo perf script > /tmp/perf.$pid.script
```

ryan: I'll run that now on a repro node. If anyone wants to watch, @jess @omar.

jess: thanks. If we get a clear backtrace that shows allocator churn at tail calls, we may try rolling back MALLOC_ARENA_MAX to the previous value.

omar: small investigation note — the OOMs only affect the canary pool (dedicated), not the hosted API. So either workload shape or the image change is needed. We should also validate the runtime build ID: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` on the image.

ria (tia): ran the bench once, attaching short diffs below (pasted):
```
# peak RSS over 120s (previous image): 9.2G
# peak RSS on current image: 17.1G
# steady qps roughly same, latency p50/p95 within 5%
```

omar: that delta is huge. Can you check `LD_PRELOAD` and `MALLOC_CONF` that the process sees?

ria (tia): `env | egrep -i "malloc|ld_preload"` output:
```
MALLOC_CONF=oversize_threshold:1,background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:30000,muzzy_decay_ms:30000,arena_max:8
LD_PRELOAD=
```

omar: arena_max:8 — that's the tunable we changed. Historically lowering arena_max reduces RSS but can increase contention. For the canary workload looks like it helped for latency earlier but now memory usage ballooned.

ana: other idea — maybe KV-cache prefix caching changed and keeps big tensors in process memory. Any recent changes to cache size? @ana can you confirm?

ana (ana): there was a PR to bump prefix cache to 6GB for canaries (PR #4098). That combined with arena changes could explain the 17GB. We should correlate which pages are anonymous vs file-backed in smaps.

jess: good point. tia/ryan — when you capture smaps please include the "AnonHugePages" lines and the RSS breakdown we can grep for `^Rss:` and `^Private_Clean:`.

ryan: perf + smaps captured. Uploading artifacts to the thread after I push to /tmp and scp to s3. Short peek: top flame shows a lot of `memcpy` / `alloc` activity in the runtime's cache eviction logic.

omar: can you run `jeprof --svg /tmp/je_stats.$pid /path/to/binary > /tmp/je.$pid.svg` and upload? svg helps see site.

ryan: done, link: https://s3.redwood-internal/test/canary-43/jeprof-1998765432.svg

jess: opening it now. Hmm looks like big allocation vectors are in `kv_cache::reserve` and `prefix_cache::hold()`; suspicious.

omar: until we have a fix, mitigation options:
1) reduce prefix cache size via env override on canary config
2) revert MALLOC_ARENA_MAX to previous value
3) add an oom-monitor to restart before kernel OOM (probe memory.high)

ana: I can push a config flip to reduce prefix cache to 2GB for canary-43 for the next 6 hours to see if it stabilizes. Want me to proceed?

jess: please do. Make it a config override in the deployment so we can roll forward quickly. Note: document the change in #deployments.

omar: I'll prepare a small PR to revert arena_max change in the runtime image and run bench in staging. If the revert reduces RSS we can roll.

ria (tia): after lowering cache size locally and rerunning the bench, peak RSS drops to ~10.1G. Latency impact small.

jess: great, thanks. Next steps summary:
- ana: confirm prefix-cache bump PR context and put rollback if needed (ana)
- nana: flip canary override to 2GB now (nana)
- omar: PR to revert arena_max change in image; bench in staging (omar)
- ryan & tia: attach full smaps/perf/jemalloc dumps to the incident ticket (ryan, tia)

ryan: will attach artifacts and mark thread when uploaded. ETA 15m.

ana: override pushed and canary redeployed (2m ago). Monitoring. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [info] deployment canary-43 config update: prefix_cache_max=2GB by nana (revision 22)

jess: monitoring shows no further OOMs in the last 12m, peak from new run ~9.8G. Looks promising. Keep the rollback PR gated until we confirm 1h of stability.

omar: logging an RFC-sized follow-up: we should add an automated integration test that runs high-concurrency prefix-cache stress for 5m on new images before canary. I'll open an issue.

jess: thanks everyone. Leaving this thread open for artifact uploads and the PR link. If OOMs resume, escalate to oncall.

ryan: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-internal/canary-43/{smaps.3129,perf.script,je_stats,je.svg}

tia: added quick note to ticket with `jeprof` findings and the bench command used.

jess: closing plan: hold the revert PR for now; keep override in place until next deploy window. Will follow up in postmortem if this reappears. :white_check_mark:
